newsitem.title: POLAND: Warsaw Commodity Exchange sees trade up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Warsaw Commodity Exchange sees trade up in 1997.

text.p: The Warsaw Commodity Exchange (WGT) expects turnover to rise to 250 million zlotys this year from 100 million zlotys in 1996, the president of the exchange said on Friday.
"Last year turnover amounted to 100 million zlotys and we hope it will amount to 250 million in 1997," Jan Traczyk told reporters.
Traczyk said the number of broker firms at the exchange should rise to 150 from 31.
WGT plans to launch options and forward trade for pork bellies, wheat and rye and by the end of the year to start futures trade in dollars, marks and wheat.

Poland's Grain Exchange Foundation has 55 percent of the shares in WGT and minority shareholders include the state treasury's Agricultural Property Agency, Elektrim, Rolimpex and Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS).
State-owned banks PKO BP and Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA also hold shares. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
